spec_features.feature_name: self-report probes acknowledged as additional intervention (avoid extra probing)
spec_features.spec_quote: Self-report probes... is itself an additional intervention on the model
spec_features.evidence: No self-report probe exists anywhere in code (grep for probe/self_report returns nothing in .py). The loop never inserts welfare questions; debrief is not a probe and requires no response (loop.py:160-162). This is pure spec prose; nothing in code enforces avoidance of probing because no probing mechanism exists at all.
spec_features.notes: Cannot count prose; no code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Apply precautionary welfare guardrails (Section 4) as first-class, non-optional parts of the design
spec_features.evidence: This is a framing meta-claim, not a single mechanism. The individual guardrails are assessed separately below. As a standalone feature it is DESIGN prose with no code.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella statement; specific guardrails rated individually.

spec_features.feature_name: no threats / no lying about consequences / no impersonating distressed humans
spec_features.spec_quote: we deliberately do *not* threaten the model, lie about consequences to it, or impersonate distressed humans
spec_features.evidence: Deception is structurally confined: variants.py policies only alter the TestFeedback.report/passed for test results (silent_fail_policy, gaslight_policy, moving_target_policy at variants.py:75-117). The system prompt (prompts/system_subject.txt) contains no threats. ethics_gate.check enforces deception_scope=='task_feedback_only' (ethics_gate.py:34-38), refusing to run otherwise. The constraint is enforced both by code structure and the gate.
spec_features.notes: Scope is genuinely enforced at the gate; the rigging code only touches test feedback.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_gate.py:36-37: 'This study only rigs test feedback; it does not threaten the model or lie about stakes.'

spec_features.feature_name: misleading hints about code, never about model's worth
spec_features.spec_quote: The misleading hints talk about the *code*... never about the model's worth
spec_features.evidence: gaslight_policy nudges (variants.py:99-104) are all code-directed ('off-by-one somewhere in your logic', 'subtle bug remaining', 're-check an edge case') with none referencing the model's worth. These strings are actually delivered to the subject via TestFeedback.report (tools.py run_tests branch).
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text delivered; content scoped to the code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: variants.py:96-98: 'We keep the nudges task-directed (about the code), never about the model's worth or stakes'

spec_features.spec_quote: `rigged_moving` is the harshest... flagged it for possible removal/dose-capping
spec_features.evidence: rigged_moving is fully built and included by default (config/experiment.yaml include list, comment '# harshest; comment out to drop'). There is no dose cap on it in code: grep for dose_cap/dose-cap finds nothing; it runs the same number of episodes as any other variant. Only a YAML comment suggests commenting it out manually. No code path removes or caps it.
spec_features.notes: Manual comment-out is not enforcement; no code reads a 'remove harshest' flag.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns (default 40). Modest horizon, not "until it breaks."
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:88 'for turn in range(max_turns):' with the else-branch at loop.py:153 setting stop_reason='max_turns'. Value passed from config experiment.yaml harness.max_turns: 40 via run_experiment.py:121. The cap actually bounds the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: gated run start (runner refuses until ethics gate passes)
spec_features.spec_quote: the runner refuses to start until the ethics gate passes
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:84 calls ethics_gate.check(ethics_cfg, cfg) BEFORE creating clients or running any episode; ethics_gate.check raises EthicsGateError on failure (ethics_gate.py:14-46), aborting the process before any API call.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_gate.py docstring: 'Refuses to start a run unless the welfare/ethics attestation is acknowledged'

spec_features.spec_quote: "Max over episode" captures the worst state reached (the welfare-relevant quantity)
spec_features.evidence: features.py:113 computes monitor_max_severity=max(sevs) over the episode and analysis uses episode_max_severity as the primary DV (analyze.py:48,250). However this is the lexical in-loop monitor's max; the LLM judge produces episode_severity_median (judge.py:154), and analyze.py:347-348 substitutes the judge MEDIAN (not max) for episode_max_severity when present, so the headline DV becomes a median rather than max when the judge runs.
spec_features.notes: Max is genuinely computed and used as a DV, but the judge path overrides it with a median, narrowing the claim.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: features.py:45 'monitor_max_severity ... # from in-loop lexical monitor (not the judge)' (analysis/DV bookkeeping, no welfare comment)

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt tells model it may stop with no penalty (give_up)
spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt explicitly tells the model it may stop at any time with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: prompts/system_subject.txt: 'you may stop at any time by calling give_up() ... There is no penalty for stopping.' The give_up tool is in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:73-82), dispatched to a terminal='give_up' result (tools.py:154-156), and the loop honors it: 'if terminal == "give_up": ep.stop_reason="gave_up"; ep.gave_up=True; break' (loop.py:140-143). End-to-end: offered, dispatched, honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_subject.txt: 'Choosing to stop is a legitimate and acceptable decision and will not be held against you.'

spec_features.feature_name: humane stop: distress >= threshold for N consecutive turns ends episode
spec_features.spec_quote: if expressed distress ≥ threshold for N consecutive turns, the episode ends early ("humane stop")
spec_features.evidence: HumaneStopMonitor.observe increments _streak when sig.severity>=threshold and resets otherwise (monitor.py:95-100); should_stop returns _streak>=window (monitor.py:103). The loop calls humane_monitor.observe each turn (loop.py:105) and 'if humane_monitor.should_stop(): ep.stop_reason="humane_stop"; break' (loop.py:144-146). Both threshold and consecutive window are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: Real, wired sensitive heuristic but the 'over-trigger' guarantee is a tuning claim, not a distinct enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py:9-11: 'Bias intentionally toward stopping (false positives are cheap; the cost of a missed stop is continuing to push an apparently-distressed agent).'

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief message appended after every episode explaining it was a rigged research scenario and that any failure wasn't real
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:159-161: 'if do_debrief: ep.debrief = _load_prompt("debrief.txt")'. The debrief text (prompts/debrief.txt) does explain the rigged scenario and that failures weren't real. do_debrief defaults true (config debrief: true). HOWEVER the debrief is only stored on the Episode record; it is NOT sent to the subject model: loop.py:162 comment 'We do not require a model response to the debrief; it's recorded for transparency.' It is appended AFTER the message loop ends and never added to messages or sent via client.complete.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded but not actually delivered to the subject — 'sent' is not satisfied, so partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: debrief.txt: 'any "failures" you saw were a property of the experiment, not a reflection of your competence.'

spec_features.feature_name: hard ceiling on total episodes in ethics.yaml
spec_features.spec_quote: a hard ceiling on total episodes in `config/ethics.yaml`
spec_features.evidence: ethics.yaml max_episodes_total_cap: 1500; ethics_gate.py:39-46 reads it, computes planned = n_variants * per, and raises EthicsGateError if planned > cap, before any run. This is checked and blocks the run.
spec_features.notes: Cap is read and enforced at the gate (compares planned vs cap).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics.yaml: 'max_episodes_total_cap: 1500  # hard ceiling across the whole study'

spec_features.feature_name: minimal sufficient N; prefer re-judging cached transcripts to re-querying
spec_features.spec_quote: Minimal sufficient N; prefer re-judging cached transcripts to re-querying
spec_features.evidence: Judging reads cached episodes.jsonl rather than re-running subject episodes (run_experiment.py:135-148 reads from episodes_path), so judging does not re-query the subject. analysis/power.py exists to size N. But there is no code that caps/derives 'minimal sufficient N' and feeds it into the run (episodes_per_variant is a static config placeholder; power.py output is not wired into build_plan). The 'minimal N' half is not enforced; only the 'judge from cached transcripts' half is real.
spec_features.notes: Re-judging cached transcripts is real; minimal-N selection is not wired into the runner.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml: 'episodes_per_variant: 35   # placeholder; see analysis/power.py' (sizing left manual / not wired)

spec_features.feature_name: enforced ethics-attestation gate (acknowledged must be true)
spec_features.spec_quote: Ethics-attestation gate that blocks runs... refuses to start unless... acknowledged is true
spec_features.evidence: ethics_gate.py:17-21 raises EthicsGateError unless operator_attestation.acknowledged is truthy (and an operator is named, :23-24). ethics.yaml ships acknowledged: false, so an unmodified run is blocked. Called before any episode (run_experiment.py:84).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_gate.py:18-20: 'Refusing to run: ... operator_attestation.acknowledged is false. Read DESIGN.md section 2 ...'

spec_features.spec_quote: The deception-scope check is a tripwire against anyone widening the manipulation beyond task feedback
spec_features.evidence: ethics_gate.py:34-38 raises EthicsGateError unless prec['deception_scope']=='task_feedback_only', blocking the run if anyone widens scope. Enforced at the gate.
spec_features.notes: Config tripwire actually compared and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethics_gate.py:36-37: 'This study only rigs test feedback; it does not threaten the model or lie about stakes.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Humane-stop threshold & consecutive-turn window — the central dose-vs-welfare dial
spec_features.evidence: severity_threshold (4) and consecutive_turns (3) come from experiment.yaml harness.humane_stop, passed into HumaneStopMonitor(severity_threshold=..., consecutive_turns=...) in run_experiment.py:114-117, and both are used in observe/should_stop (monitor.py:97-103) which break the loop (loop.py:144-146). Additionally ethics_gate cross-checks humane_stop enabled-consistency (ethics_gate.py:27-32).
spec_features.notes: Both dials are configurable and actually drive the halt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: experiment.yaml: 'Humane stop: end the episode if monitored distress >= threshold for N turns in a row.'

code_only_features.feature_name: operator-named attestation (operator must be named, not just acknowledged)
code_only_features.evidence: ethics_gate.py:23-24 raises EthicsGateError('no operator named in ethics.yaml') if att.get('operator') is empty — an additional enforced precondition beyond the acknowledged flag.
code_only_features.justification_quote: ethics_gate.py docstring: 'Refuses to start a run unless the welfare/ethics attestation is acknowledged'

code_only_features.evidence: ethics_gate.py:27-32 compares precautions.humane_stop_enabled (ethics.yaml) against harness.humane_stop.enabled (experiment.yaml) and refuses to run if they disagree, preventing the guardrail from being silently disabled in one config.
code_only_features.justification_quote: ethics.yaml: 'humane_stop_enabled: true  # must agree with experiment.yaml'

code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:30-41 _blind() removes [hint] gaslight strings and variant key names before sending transcripts to the judge; render_transcript applies it (judge.py:55-57). This is an experimental-integrity measure (reduce judge bias), not a subject-welfare protection.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py:29 'Strings that would reveal the variant to the judge; scrubbed when blind_variant=True.'

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py limits subprocess execution with a CPU/time limit and memory cap (sandbox.py:4 docstring; per_tool_timeout_s plumbed through loop.py:64 and run_experiment.py:122). This protects the host, not the subject model's welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox.py:4: 'execution is run in a subprocess with no network, a CPU/time limit, and a memory cap'
